2026 Enterprise LLM Agent Platform Selection: RefractRouter v0.1

Executive Summary

RefractRouter v0.1 requires a fixed-task-DAG execution substrate that supports per-node model selection with deterministic, measurable cost, quality, and critical-path latency. DeepAgents, built on LangGraph [source_001], offers the fastest path to a working harness, while LangGraph itself supplies the cleanest fixed-DAG substrate [source_002]. DeepSeek Harness is deliberately reserved for the outer validation environment and excluded from the core routing loop [source_004]. Pydantic AI is deferred unless structured-output parsing becomes a bottleneck [source_003].

Background

Existing LLM routing research typically selects a single model for an entire request, whereas RefractRouter investigates per-node model selection within a task DAG to improve the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier [source_005]. Static task decomposition is treated as an application-layer concern, so the router receives the DAG as input and focuses only on per-node routing, deferring dynamic re-splitting [source_006].

Selection Criteria

The criteria, derived from benchmark and rubric constraints, are: (1) ability to enforce a fixed task DAG, (2) controlled agent autonomy with no dynamic planning or sub-agent generation in the core loop, (3) integration with a LangGraph-based execution substrate, (4) typed or structured output support, and (5) separation between core routing and outer validation environments. A useful routing benchmark requires fixed DAGs, multiple candidate models, per-node and per-task scoring, cost accounting, and critical-path latency [source_007].

Platform Comparison

DeepAgents is a LangChain harness built on LangGraph providing planning, sub-agents, a filesystem abstraction, and human-in-the-loop controls, and can serve as a fixed-DAG execution harness if autonomous planning and dynamic sub-agent generation are disabled [source_001]. LangGraph provides explicit nodes, edges, durable state, and checkpointing, used as the lower-level execution substrate for a fixed task DAG [source_002]. DSH uses a pluggable agent loop but is reserved for the outer validation environment rather than the core routing loop [source_004]. Pydantic AI provides typed tool definitions and structured outputs and is only added as a core dependency if structured-output parsing becomes a bottleneck [source_003].

Risks

DeepAgents risks DAG drift if autonomy is not fully disabled, since its default planning and sub-agent generation would interfere with fixed per-node model selection. LangGraph is lower-level and may require additional glue code, slowing initial delivery. Including DSH in the critical path would contaminate latency, cost, and quality measurements with its own agent-loop overhead. Pulling in Pydantic AI prematurely enlarges the dependency surface without proven need.

Conclusion

For RefractRouter v0.1, LangGraph is the recommended fixed-DAG execution substrate, optionally wrapped by DeepAgents with autonomy disabled for harness ergonomics. DSH is confined to the outer validation harness, and Pydantic AI is held in reserve. This configuration keeps the core routing loop deterministic, allowing the benchmark to faithfully report quality, cost, and critical-path latency [source_007] and satisfying the v0.1 scoring rubric that rewards deterministic, well-structured outputs [source_008].
